questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I've been to Berlin a lot of times before, and it was nice to me to be a place i knew i a bit before I came.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Most of it just came on KU-mail, so that was nice

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: People that read in the Philology department where really nice to help

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was a bit difficult, it helped a lot for me to do a post on facebook groups.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: For me it was nice living off campus, because my uni was a bit out of the city. I would rather live a bit more central and have a bit longer to uni. In general I would say, because Berlin is so big, it's important to think about location if it's possible. I lived in Charlottenburg, which is a really nice and quite area, but also around an hour away from the areas in Berlin I like the most and a bit difficult to come around. So I think it's important to keep in mind.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I think I had to fill out some documents. But they where really sweet to help on the orientation days and in generell at the university. There are a lot of places you can go if you have questions.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: At the uni there where some 'stations' where you could go if you had questions and for the whole week of orientation days you could also always ask.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted, but the system of registering for the classes was very confusing to be honest .

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't be afraid to ask questions because everyone is confused

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I chose a lot of courses for exchange students and most of them where really interesting and a nice way to get to know new people. The only thing was that our level of german where really different, which sometimes made it a bit difficult to make the courses interesting for everyone. Other than that I had some lectures in literature which was also nice.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I had a Spionage kurs for exchange students that was really interesting, it was mostly about espionage during the cold war. The lectures where also nice, I had one called "Einführung in die neuere deutsche Literatur' that was really interesting

questions.answer: I didn't try anything at the university and didn't really look into it. I think there were a lot of social activities, but I found it in other contexts than uni

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Clubbing! And just exploring the city

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There are in general a lot of nice museums in Mitte and then I really like the areas Friedrichshain and Prenzlauer Berg. There are a lot of nice cafes, flea markets and bars

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: A bit difficult for me, it was easier for me to meet other exchange students maybe also because of my courses.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Maybe choose some courses that aren’t only for exchange students

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be prepared that it's going to be confusing in the beginning, but it will very much be worth it and there are a lot of people you can ask.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being more independent and get to know a lot of new people not only from Germany but all around the world.
